questions.question: When using context clues, what should a reader examine?
choices: nearby words and ideas that help explain an unfamiliar word

questions.question: In “The trail was arduous; after miles of climbing, we were exhausted,” what does “arduous” most likely mean?
“The glass was fragile, so Luis wrapped it in cloth.” What does “fragile” most likely mean?
“Unlike her outgoing brother, Maya was reserved at the gathering.” What does “reserved” most likely mean?
“The forecast predicted a deluge, and streets quickly flooded.” What does “deluge” most likely mean?
The author calls the old bridge “sturdy” and says it remained firm in strong winds. What does “sturdy” mean here?
“After the team’s victory, the coach praised their tenacity during setbacks.” What does “tenacity” most likely mean?
“The directions were concise: four short steps explained the task.” What does “concise” mean?
The scientist’s claim was “tentative”; she said more trials were needed. What does “tentative” mean?
“Although the hallway looked chaotic, the teacher’s notes showed an orderly plan.” What does “chaotic” most likely mean?
A reader encounters “The author’s tone was somber; the passage focused on loss and used restrained language.” What does “somber” suggest?
A character is described as “meticulous,” checking each measurement twice before cutting. What does this context imply?
“Her explanation was ambiguous, so listeners disagreed about what she meant.” What does “ambiguous” mean?
choices: open to more than one interpretation

questions.question: “The old map was obsolete after new roads were built.” What does “obsolete” mean?
“Despite the setback, the group remained optimistic and planned another attempt.” What does “optimistic” mean?
Which clue most strongly helps explain “parched” in “After hours without water, the hikers felt parched”?
choices: the hikers had gone without water

questions.question: A word’s connotation is its what?
“Lean” and “skinny” can refer to a similar body shape but differ in what?
A student guesses a word’s meaning from one nearby adjective, ignoring the rest of the paragraph. What should the student do?
choices: use the whole sentence and surrounding ideas to check the guess

questions.question: A passage uses “vital” for an action needed to prevent failure. Which meaning fits best?
